question: Assume today is 2026-08-16. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan in August 2026, as it will be first reported in the Japan National Tourism Organization's (JNTO) monthly estimate.

target.what: Number of foreign visitor arrivals to Japan (inbound international visitors) as estimated by the Japan National Tourism Organization (JNTO) for the calendar month of August 2026. This is a count of visits (arrivals), not unique individuals, based on immigration records and JNTO's estimation methodol
target.cadence: monthly, typically released around the 15th-20th of the following month
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the information cutoff (2026-08-16). The estimate is for the full month of August 2026, but only data up to mid-August may be available at the cutoff. JNTO's monthly estimate is based on immigration arrivals and may be revised. candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 arrivals can be projected from the same month in previous years, adjusted for recent growth trends and seasonality. The year-over-year growth rate in recent months, if stable, can be applied to August 2025 arrivals to estimate August 2026.
candidates.data_to_find: JNTO monthly foreign visitor arrivals for August 2023, August 2024, August 2025, and the most recent months available before the cutoff (e.g., June 2026, July 2026 if published). Also, year-over-year growth rates for these months.

candidates.hypothesis: Foreign visitor arrivals are strongly correlated with international passenger arrivals at Japanese airports. If international passenger arrival data for August 2026 (or partial data) is available, it can be used to estimate the share of foreign visitors among all international arrivals, then scaled to the full month.
candidates.data_to_find: International passenger arrivals at major Japanese airports (Narita, Haneda, Kansai, etc.) for August 2026 (or July/August partial), and the historical ratio of foreign visitor arrivals to total international passenger arrivals.
search_hints: Japan airport arrivals foreign visitors ratio

candidates.hypothesis: Seat capacity on international flights to Japan, multiplied by an estimated load factor and the share of foreign visitors, provides an upper bound or estimate. Booking data and forward-looking schedules can indicate demand.
candidates.data_to_find: International flight seat capacity to Japan for August 2026 (from OAG or airline schedules), load factors, and the proportion of seats occupied by foreign visitors. Also, hotel booking data or travel agency bookings for August 2026.
search_hints: Japan hotel bookings August 2026 foreign tourists

candidates.hypothesis: Any major events (e.g., visa policy changes, natural disasters, pandemics, economic shocks, currency fluctuations) between the cutoff and August 2026 could affect arrivals. The impact can be estimated by comparing to similar past events.
candidates.data_to_find: News about Japan travel advisories, visa policy changes, currency exchange rates (JPY), and any major disruptions (e.g., typhoons, earthquakes) affecting travel in August 2026. Also, historical impact of similar events on monthly arrivals.

candidates.hypothesis: Official forecasts or targets for Japan's inbound tourism in 2026, such as from the Japan Tourism Agency or JNTO, can provide a baseline. If a full-year target exists, monthly seasonality can allocate it to August.
candidates.data_to_find: Japan Tourism Agency's inbound tourism forecasts for 2026, JNTO's targets, or industry forecasts (e.g., from travel associations). Also, any prediction market or analyst estimates for August 2026 arrivals.

candidates.hypothesis: August is typically a peak month for Japanese outbound and inbound tourism due to summer holidays. The share of August arrivals in the annual total can be used with a full-year estimate. Also, major source markets (e.g., South Korea, China, Taiwan, USA) have distinct patterns that can be summed.
candidates.data_to_find: Historical monthly seasonality indices for Japan inbound tourism (e.g., August share of annual arrivals), and recent trends in arrivals from top source countries for summer 2026.
search_hints: Japan visitor arrivals by country August 2025

candidates.hypothesis: Immigration entry records for August 2026 (if available in real-time or preliminary) can directly provide the count. Even partial data for early August can be extrapolated.
candidates.data_to_find: Preliminary immigration entry counts for foreign nationals at Japanese ports of entry for August 2026 (or July 2026 if August not yet available). Also, daily or weekly arrival counts from airport authorities.

candidates.hypothesis: Online search interest for Japan travel (e.g., Google Trends) correlates with actual arrivals with a lead time. If search interest for August 2026 travel is known, it can indicate demand strength relative to previous years.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends data for 'Japan travel' or similar queries for the period leading up to August 2026, compared to previous years. Also, social media mentions or travel app downloads.

assessment.note: All five points describe the same JNTO June 2026 release: foreign visitor arrivals fell 6.8% year-on-year to 3.15 million, while 15 markets set June records. p4, p13, p27 and p52 are redundant restatements of the same 15-market record count from the same underlying JNTO release; they are not independent confirmations. p2 supplies the only June 2026 level/change information and is the key recent momentum indicator.

These are all from the JNTO January 2026 annual/December release and describe the strength of 2025 inbound tourism: 7 markets set single-month records in December 2025, 14 set December records, 7 markets exceeded 1 million annual arrivals, and 20 markets set annual records. They are mutually consistent and establish a high 2025 base, but they are not independent of each other and do not directly measure August 2026.

June 2026 arrivals were down 6.8% year-on-year despite many market records, implying the 2025 base was exceptionally strong and/or some large source markets (notably China) weakened. This is a material tension for any August 2026 forecast: broad-based market strength coexists with an aggregate year-on-year decline.

The range 0.95-1.40 reflects uncertainty about whether the June decline persists or reverses during the summer peak.

assumptions.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 arrivals were below June 2026 levels, or that the June 2026 decline was driven by a one-off factor that reversed sharply in August.

kept.name: August 2026 foreign visitor arrivals relative to June 2026 arrivals
kept.rationale: August is typically a summer peak month for Japan inbound tourism, with arrivals often 10-20% above June. June 2026 was 3.15 million (p2). A ratio of 1.15 is a central summer uplift, with wide uncertainty reflecting possible continuation of the June YoY decline and unknown policy or demand shocks.
kept.applies_when: The seasonal pattern from recent normal years (2023-2025) holds and no major new shock occurs between June and August 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 arrivals were below June 2026 levels, or that a major shock (e.g., new travel restrictions, natural disaster) suppressed summer travel.

kept.name: August 2026 foreign visitor arrivals relative to August 2025 arrivals
kept.rationale: June 2026 was down 6.8% YoY (p2), suggesting a possible slowdown. August 2026 may be slightly below August 2025, but summer peak demand and record market strength (p4) could offset. A ratio of 0.95 with wide uncertainty reflects this tension.
kept.applies_when: The YoY decline observed in June 2026 persists into August 2026, but no severe deterioration occurs.
kept.falsified_by: Evidence that August 2026 arrivals exceeded August 2025, or that the decline deepened substantially.

Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.

Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.

ablation.rule: exclude points from own_history directions and points whose name contains a target entity anchor and whose name or unit shares a stem with the target unit (triangulate/agent/ablation.py)
residual_risks: Own values named by an alias or abbreviation, or with no entity in the point name, are not excluded.

The rule over-excludes on purpose: any point naming the target entity together with the target quantity (for example a survey of the target's visitors) is excluded, even when it is not a value of the target itself.
The model's own memory of the target's history is not removed: it can still shape the plan, the judge's choices and assumption values.
The searcher and the extractor still see pages that contain own values; only the judge's table is filtered.
